connections.observation: ἀκολουθέω (s002) and ἕπομαι (s003) together construct a hierarchical chain of following that unfolds through the section: harmony and rhythm must follow λόγος (398d), λόγος itself must follow the ἦθος of the soul (400d), λέξις follows that ἦθος, rhythm and harmony follow λέξις (400d), the foot must be forced to follow λόγος (400a), and εὐσχημοσύνη follows εὔρυθμον (400c). Held together, the two verb families make visible a single transitive movement from psychic character through speech to musical form, with each stage compelling the next.

The three-part definition of μέλος (λόγος, ἁρμονία, ῥυθμός, s001) is enacted through the hierarchical following articulated by ἀκολουθέω and ἕπομαι (s002, s003): harmony and rhythm are declared to follow λόγος (398d), and the section proceeds to treat each element in the sequence announced—first λόγος and its relation to prior τύποι, then harmonies, then rhythms—making the announced structure perform itself through the order of treatment and the subordination repeatedly asserted.

The βίαιον/ἑκούσιον pairing (s004) selects exactly two harmonies from the rejected sequence of named modes (s005): after removing θρηνώδεις and μαλακαί/συμποτικαί modes, Dorian and Phrygian remain, which are then explicitly named as βίαιον and ἑκούσιον harmonies. The contrast makes visible that the selection operates through a single binary opposition of force and willing action, reducing multiplicity to duality.

The five εὐ- compounds clustered at 400d–e (εὐλογία, εὐαρμοστία, εὐσχημοσύνη, εὐρυθμία, εὐήθεια, s006) are immediately set against three paired ἀ-/εὐ- contrasts (s007: εὐσχημοσύνη/ἀσχημοσύνη, εὔρυθμος/ἄρρυθμος, εὐάρμοστος/ἀνάρμοστος). Together they make visible a double structure: the εὐ- cluster gathers good qualities in several domains as siblings that all follow εὐήθεια, while the paired contrasts articulate the same domains as binary oppositions, showing goodness and badness as mutually exclusive alternatives that extend through every technical dimension just examined.

The Apollo/Marsyas judgment (s008) is enacted through the πολυ-/παν- multiplicity terms (s009): the rejected instruments—triangles, pektides, aulos—are characterized as πολύχορδα, πολυαρμόνια, with the aulos called πολυχορδότατον and a μίμημα of τὰ παναρμόνια, while the retained instruments—lyre and kithara—are Apollo's. The conjunction makes visible that the divine/satyr opposition is performed as a choice between simplicity and multiplicity of strings and modes.

μιμέομαι/μίμημα (s010) moves from harmony imitating a brave man's tones (399a), to the aulos as imitation of παναρμόνια (399d), to rhythms as imitations of lives (400a), to good form as imitations of good ἦθος (401a), then the ἔρως vocabulary (s019) clusters at the close where μουσική is said to terminate in τὰ τοῦ καλοῦ ἐρωτικά (403c). Together they make visible that imitation moves upward through technical strata until it reaches its τέλος in eros, where the μουσικός loves the most beautiful person and ὀρθὸς ἔρως loves μουσικῶς.

The purifying vocabulary (s011: καθαίρω, διακαθαίρω at 399e) and the nourishing/training vocabulary (s013: τρυφάω, τρέφω, τροφή) intersect at the recognition that the city called luxurious (τρυφᾶν) is being purified (διακαθαίροντες). The section then proceeds to describe proper τροφή in μουσική that produces one who is καλός τε κἀγαθός. Held together, they make visible that purgation and cultivation operate on the same city: removing bad elements and providing good nourishment are twin aspects of the same formative regime.

The contrasting environmental images (s014: κακῇ βοτάνῃ versus ὑγιεινῷ τόπῳ, with αὔρα carrying health from good places) and the downward/inward movement vocabulary (s015: καταδύεται εἰς τὸ ἐντὸς τῆς ψυχῆς, καταδεχόμενος εἰς τὴν ψυχήν) together make visible two reciprocal movements: rhythm and harmony sink down into the soul's interior while a breeze brings health from without, so that cultivation happens both through what enters the soul from beautiful works and through what musical training deposits within.

The letters analogy (s016: recognizing στοιχεῖα and their εἰκόνες enables recognition of virtue εἴδη and their images) and the συμφωνία vocabulary (s027: consistency with prior agreements, consonance of soul with καλὸς λόγος, accord between ἦθος and bodily εἶδος) together make visible that the capacity to recognize forms everywhere—whether letters or virtues—is simultaneously a capacity for συμφωνία: the same τέχνη and μελέτη that lets one see recurrent patterns also produces inner and outer consonance, making recognition and harmony aspects of the same μουσική formation.

The opening announcement of what remains (s017: τὸ περὶ ᾠδῆς τρόπου καὶ μελῶν λοιπόν at 398c) and the closing declaration of τέλος (s017: the λόγος about μουσική has reached its end, which must terminate εἰς τὰ τοῦ καλοῦ ἐρωτικά at 403c) frame the ἔρως cluster (s019: ἐρασμιώτατον, ὁ μουσικὸς ἐρῴη, ὀρθὸς ἔρως, ἐρωτικά). Together they make visible that the entire movement through harmonies, rhythms, and instruments arrives at a τέλος already implicit in μουσική itself: eros of the beautiful, where the μουσικός loves what is καλός and the discussion reaches completion by naming its own erotic aim.

The ἀδελφά recurrence (s018: bad form and bad speech are siblings, good form and good character are siblings and imitations, virtues are siblings) together with the εὐ- cluster (s006) and the εὐ-/ἀ- contrasts (s007) make visible a double kinship structure: virtues are named as ἀδελφά to one another, and good formal qualities (εὐσχημοσύνη, εὐρυθμία, εὐαρμοστία) are called both ἀδελφά and μιμήματα of good ἦθος, while their opposed bad qualities are likewise siblings of bad character. The siblingship extends horizontally among virtues and vertically between psychic and formal domains.

The σωφροσύνη/excessive pleasure contrast (s020: ἡδονή ὑπερβαλλούσα is ἔκφρων and μανική, especially τὰ ἀφροδίσια) immediately precedes the ἔρως conclusion (s019: ὀρθὸς ἔρως loves κοσμίου τε καὶ καλοῦ σωφρόνως τε καὶ μουσικῶς, and μουσική terminates εἰς τὰ τοῦ καλοῦ ἐρωτικά). Together they make visible that the τέλος of μουσική in eros is articulated through exclusion: right eros is defined against μανία and ἀκολασία, and the highest pleasure—sexual pleasure—is declared incompatible with σωφροσύνη and thus absent from the eros that constitutes μουσική's completion.

λείπω recurs as the operative verb throughout the selection process (s023: harmonies, instruments, and rhythms are each 'left' or 'retained'), and this vocabulary structures the sequential elimination of named modes (s005: θρηνώδεις, then μαλακαί/συμποτικαί are removed, leaving Dorian and Phrygian). Together they make visible that construction of the μουσική curriculum proceeds through subtraction rather than addition: what will educate is what remains after removal, and λείπω names both the act of exclusion and the residue that survives it.

The dense series of verbal adjectives in -τέον/-τέα (s025: ἀφαιρετέαι, διωκτέα, ἐπιστατητέον, προσαναγκαστέον, διακωλυτέον, ἐατέος, προσοιστέον) articulates a regime of compulsion applied to the δημιουργοί recurrence (s026: makers of instruments will not be maintained, all craftsmen must be supervised, those who cannot track the beautiful must not be allowed to work in the city, but certain craftsmen must be sought). Together they make visible that the selection of good forms requires legislative control over production: necessity-language specifies what must and must not be done, and craftsmen are the object of that necessity, either excluded or compelled.

Glaucon's disclaimer (s021: he laughs and declares himself ἐκτὸς τῶν πάντων, unable to answer what is needed) is answered by Socrates' own disclaimers (s022: οὐκ οἶδα τὰς ἁρμονίας, will consult Damon, heard things οὐ σαφῶς), yet both proceed to supply answers—Glaucon names the rejected modes, Socrates specifies the two retained harmonies and the principle governing rhythms. Together they make visible a pattern of claimed ignorance followed by substantive specification, making the disavowal of expertise into a repeated gesture that frames rather than prevents the determination of what μουσική requires.

The βίαιον/ἑκούσιον pairing (s004) specifies two harmonies that will μιμήσαιτο the tones and inflections of a brave man in war or peacetime action (s010), and μίμημα recurs to describe rhythms as imitations of lives (400a) and good formal qualities as imitations of good ἦθος (401a). Together they make visible that the two retained harmonies are not arbitrary survivals but the minimal pair needed to imitate the two fundamental modes of virtuous action—forced and willing—and that imitation operates as the linking principle between βίος, ἦθος, and the technical forms of melody and rhythm.

Socrates' oath νὴ τὸν κύνα (s012) occurs precisely at the moment he recognizes λελήθαμέν γε διακαθαίροντες the city called luxurious (s011). The oath marks the recognition itself as something that has escaped notice: they have been purifying without realizing it. The conjunction makes visible that the purification is simultaneous with the λόγος about μουσική and is disclosed rather than initiated by Socrates' self-aware exclamation.

The city/country distribution of instruments (s024: lyre and kithara κατὰ πόλιν, syrinx κατʼ ἀγροὺς for herdsmen) follows immediately upon the Apollo/Marsyas judgment (s008). Together they make visible that the divine/satyr choice is also an urban/rural distribution: Apollo's instruments belong to the city, while the rural instrument—associated with pastoral life—is neither Apollo's nor Marsyas' but a third term, located spatially outside the πόλις and assigned to νομεῖς.

elements.context: οὐ πρότερον γνωσόμεθα, πρὶν ἂν αὐτὰ γνῶμεν ... οὐδὲ μουσικοὶ πρότερον ἐσόμεθα ... πρὶν ἂν τὰ τῆς σωφροσύνης εἴδη ... γνωρίζωμεν

new_signals.observation: πρὶν ἂν recurs in the double analogy structure, marking the temporal threshold before which recognition is impossible: one cannot know letter-images before knowing letters themselves, and cannot be μουσικοί before recognizing the εἴδη of virtues everywhere they appear.

elements.context: οὐ πρότερον γνωσόμεθα, πρὶν ἂν αὐτὰ γνῶμεν
ἀσπάζοιτʼ ἂν αὐτὸν γνωρίζων διʼ οἰκειότητα

new_signals.observation: γιγνώσκω and γνωρίζω alternate in the letters-virtues analogy passage: future γνωσόμεθα and aorist subjunctive γνῶμεν for knowing letters, present subjunctive γνωρίζωμεν for recognizing virtue-forms, and participle γνωρίζων for the one who recognizes λόγος through oikeiotes when it arrives. The variation in tense and verb makes knowledge and recognition into distinct yet related acts.

elements.context: εἰς ὁμοιότητά τε καὶ φιλίαν καὶ συμφωνίαν

new_signals.observation: οἰκειότης appears twice: first as the outcome of musical formation alongside ὁμοιότης, φιλία, and συμφωνία with καλὸς λόγος (401d), then as the ground through which the properly trained person recognizes (γνωρίζων) λόγος when it arrives (402a). The term links the formative process to the act of recognition.

elements.context: πρὶν λόγον δυνατὸς εἶναι λαβεῖν, ἐλθόντος δὲ τοῦ λόγου ἀσπάζοιτʼ ἂν αὐτὸν γνωρίζων διʼ οἰκειότητα

new_signals.observation: λόγος is described as something that arrives (ἐλθόντος) to one already trained in μουσική, who greets it (ἀσπάζοιτο) through recognition born of kinship (γνωρίζων διʼ οἰκειότητα). The arrival is positioned after the young person has already learned to praise and hate rightly, making λόγος a latecomer to a formation already underway.

elements.context: τὰ δʼ αἰσχρὰ ψέγοι τʼ ἂν ὀρθῶς καὶ μισοῖ ἔτι νέος ὤν, πρὶν λόγον δυνατὸς εἶναι λαβεῖν

new_signals.observation: The properly trained young person praises the beautiful and hates the shameful while still young (ἔτι νέος ὤν), before being able to grasp λόγος (πρὶν λόγον δυνατὸς εἶναι λαβεῖν). The temporal priority makes right affective response precede rational capacity.

elements.context: τὰ στοιχεῖα ... ἐν ἅπασιν οἷς ἔστιν περιφερόμενα
τὰ τῆς σωφροσύνης εἴδη ... πανταχοῦ περιφερόμενα

new_signals.observation: περιφέρω recurs in identical participial form in both halves of the letters-virtues analogy: letters are carried around (περιφερόμενα) in all the places they occur, and the εἴδη of virtues are carried around everywhere (πανταχοῦ περιφερόμενα). The exact repetition binds the two terms of the analogy.

elements.context: οὐ πρότερον ἐσόμενοι γραμματικοὶ πρὶν οὕτως ἔχοιμεν

new_signals.observation: The future participle ἐσόμενοι γραμματικοί and the future verb μουσικοὶ ἐσόμεθα are set in parallel grammatical constructions, each negated by οὐ πρότερον and followed by πρίν clauses specifying the condition of competence. The parallel makes becoming γραμματικός and becoming μουσικός structurally identical achievements.
